object_description: low-rise complex of six parallel pavilion rows
design_condition: Set back in the existing orchard, the low-rise complex follows a horizontal base across the slope, recreates the walled garden and uses interior courtyards to connect the buildings with the park and surrounding landscape.

positive.statement: The low pavilion form integrates harmoniously into the rural village, castle and park.

position.rationale: Six low parallel pavilion rows are clearly visible across the plan and all elevations.

positive.statement: The irregular exterior outline blends into the landscape while the regular solids-and-voids pattern supports variety and orientation.

position.rationale: The stepped outer perimeter and repeated solids-and-voids pattern are directly visible in plan and elevations.

positive.statement: The ground-floor interior street structures the different functions favorably and provides landmarks and natural light.

position.rationale: Ground-level circulation is inferred between the parallel rows and constrained by the lowest elevation band.

positive.statement: The accommodation units offer high-quality strolling spaces and a variety of living spaces.

position.rationale: Repeated pavilion intervals and connecting open strips visibly create varied walking and living zones.

positive.statement: The restored vegetable garden and diversified outdoor program support daily contact and exchanges between inhabitants and residents.

position.target: restored vegetable garden and outdoor program
position.rationale: Landscape programming is not separately modeled; the peripheral southern-western open area is the closest anchor.

positive.statement: The low elevation allows the castle roofs to emerge and avoids competition with the historic complex.

position.target: low elevation and castle roof visibility
position.rationale: The consistently low profile is directly confirmed by the compact vertical spread in every elevation.

negative.statement: The first-floor interior street tends to separate the functions rather than structure them.

position.rationale: Upper circulation is approximated between pavilion rows at the upper repeated elevation bands.

negative.statement: The upper accommodation level is divided into two distant centers and is too compressed in places.

position.rationale: The upper row organization and its divided pavilion centers are visible in plan and upper elevation bands.

negative.statement: The bathrooms and their access are poorly designed.

position.rationale: Bathrooms are not identifiable; a representative upper accommodation bay is used as a constrained anchor.

negative.statement: The constructive principles should be specified at the level of the supporting structure and facade.

position.rationale: The repeated external facade edges are visible, though structural principles are not distinguishable.

negative.statement: The multiplied gable roofs almost produce the opposite of the intended village integration.

position.rationale: Repeated roof ridges and pavilion caps are clearly visible across the top and elevation views.

negative.statement: The project lacks a clear entry gesture and the street-side clearance needed for proper functioning.

position.rationale: An entry is not singled out; the southern exterior edge is the most plausible public approach surface.

negative.statement: The building has a large influence on the plot, a significant built volume and an introverted attitude toward public space.

position.rationale: The broad repeated footprint visibly occupies much of the sampled plan.

negative.statement: The management of the topography at the car park and underground access is poorly regulated.

position.rationale: Parking access is absent from the point cloud; the southern-eastern lower perimeter is used as an approximation.

negative.statement: The spread of the project and extensive horizontal circulation increase the accommodation area beyond target.

position.rationale: Long parallel circulation gaps and the spread of rows are directly visible in plan.

negative.statement: The multiplicity of roofs places the project toward the higher end of the cost range.

position.rationale: The repeated gabled roof geometry is directly represented throughout the model.

negative.statement: The underground car park has a significant impact on the total cost.

position.rationale: The underground garage is not visible; a lower southern-eastern footprint location is assigned.
